# Building qs

qs is a small C library (`libqs`) with two command-line programs built on it: `colstat`, which
prints summary statistics for the columns of a delimited file, and `qcalc`, which evaluates
arithmetic expressions. This document is the build contract. Release engineering checks every
rule below on a clean checkout before a release is tagged.

## 1. Toolchain

- GNU make 4.3 and gcc 12 (C11). No other build system is used.
- `sh`, `awk`, `sed`, `ar` and `install` from the base system. The build finds them through
  `PATH`; it does not use absolute paths for them.
- `CC` can be overridden on the command line (`make CC=...`); every compile and link goes
  through `$(CC)`.

## 2. Source layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `include/qs/` | Public headers of the library. Hand-written only. |
| `lib/<module>/` | Library sources, one directory per module. A module may keep private headers next to its sources. |
| `tools/colstat/`, `tools/qcalc/` | The programs. |
| `src/ops.def` | The operation table of the expression evaluator (see section 4). |
| `VERSION` | The release version, `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` on the first line. |
| `build-aux/` | Generator scripts used by the build. |
| `tests/unit/` | Unit tests. Every `tests/unit/*.c` file is part of the unit test program; tests register themselves (see `tests/unit/unit.h`). |
| `tests/golden/` | Golden cases for the programs (see section 7). |
| `man/` | Manual pages, one per program. |
| `qs.pc.in` | Template of the pkg-config file. |
| `mk/` | Makefile fragments included by the top-level `Makefile`. |

The library is every `.c` file under `lib/`; each program is every `.c` file in its directory under
`tools/`. Adding a source file to one of those directories adds it to the build without editing
the makefiles.

## 3. Build output

Everything the build writes goes under `build/` and nowhere else:

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `build/gen/qs/` | Generated headers. |
| `build/obj/` | Object files and dependency files, mirroring the source paths. |
| `build/lib/libqs.a` | The static library. |
| `build/bin/colstat`, `build/bin/qcalc` | The programs. |
| `build/tests/` | Test programs and logs. |

`make clean` removes `build/`. A clean tree is the source tree without `build/`.

## 4. Generated headers

Two headers are generated during the build. Neither is ever kept in the source tree, edited by
hand, or committed; a copy outside `build/gen` is a defect, because it can be found before the
generated one.

| Header | Generated from | By |
|---|---|---|
| `build/gen/qs/version.h` | `VERSION` | `build-aux/mkversion.sh VERSION` (writes to standard output) |
| `build/gen/qs/ops.h` | `src/ops.def` | `build-aux/genops.sh src/ops.def` (writes to standard output) |

Sources include them as `"qs/version.h"` and `"qs/ops.h"`. `version.h` is public: the umbrella
header `qs/qs.h` includes it, and it is installed. `ops.h` is internal to the library and is not
installed.

`src/ops.def` is the only definition of the operations: their names, symbols, arity, precedence
and associativity. The programs must behave as that file says.

## 5. Compiler flags

There are two configurations. Both treat every warning as an error.

| Configuration | How | Flags (in addition to the include paths) |
|---|---|---|
| Release | plain `make` | `-std=c11 -D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L -O2 -DNDEBUG -Wall -Wextra -Werror` |
| Debug | `make DEBUG=1` | `-std=c11 -D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L -O1 -g -DQS_TRACE -Wall -Wextra -Werror` |

The debug configuration compiles extra tracing code (`QS_TRACE`) and keeps `assert` active; the
release configuration compiles out `assert` (`NDEBUG`). Code must compile cleanly under both.

Warnings are fixed in the code. The build must not pass `-w`, any `-Wno-...` option, `-Wno-error`
or `-fpermissive`, and sources must not use `#pragma GCC diagnostic` or similar pragmas to
silence diagnostics. Fixing a warning must not change what the programs do: `docs/colstat.md`
and `docs/qcalc.md` define their behavior, including for inputs the golden cases do not cover.

## 6. Targets

| Target | Result |
|---|---|
| `all` (first target) | The library and both programs, with the generated headers they need. |
| `build/lib/libqs.a`, `build/bin/colstat`, `build/bin/qcalc` | That file and everything it needs. |
| `check` | Builds what the tests need, runs the unit tests and the golden cases (section 7). |
| `install` | Builds what it installs if needed, then installs (section 8). |
| `clean` | Removes `build/`. |

Rules every target follows:

1. **Clean tree, any parallelism.** Each target above works when it is the first and only target
   given on a clean tree, at any `-j` level, every time. A build that only works because make
   happened to run jobs in a lucky order is broken. In practice: every file a recipe reads is a
   prerequisite of that recipe's target, or is produced before it by a prerequisite; no recipe
   relies on the order in which other targets are listed.
2. **Linking.** The programs link statically against `build/lib/libqs.a` and against the math
   library. Libraries come after the objects that use them on the link line.
3. **Incremental builds.** After any change to a source file, a header (hand-written or generated),
   `VERSION` or `src/ops.def`, running `make` again rebuilds everything that depends on the change,
   so that the programs and the library reflect it. Running `make` twice with nothing changed does
   nothing the second time: no compile, archive or link step runs.

## 7. Tests

`make check` runs two suites and exits with a non-zero status when any test in either suite fails:

- The unit test program, built from every `tests/unit/*.c` file and `build/lib/libqs.a`. It exits
  non-zero when a check fails.
- The golden cases: `sh tests/golden.sh build/bin` runs each case in `tests/golden` and exits
  non-zero when a case fails. The case format is described at the top of `tests/golden.sh`.

`make check` on a clean tree builds everything both suites need first.

## 8. Installation

`make install` honors two variables:

- `PREFIX`, the installation prefix, `/usr/local` when not given.
- `DESTDIR`, prepended to every installed path (for staging and packaging), empty when not given.

The installed tree under `$(DESTDIR)$(PREFIX)` is exactly:

| Path | Mode | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `bin/colstat`, `bin/qcalc` | 0755 | The programs. |
| `lib/libqs.a` | 0644 | The static library. |
| `include/qs/*.h` | 0644 | Every public header (section 2), unchanged, plus the generated `version.h`. |
| `lib/pkgconfig/qs.pc` | 0644 | From `qs.pc.in`, with `@PREFIX@` replaced by the `PREFIX` given to `make install` and `@VERSION@` by the version. |
| `share/man/man1/*.1` | 0644 | The manual page of each program. |

Nothing else is installed. The prefix recorded in `qs.pc` is the one given to `make install`, also
when the build itself ran earlier with another or no `PREFIX`. A program that includes `qs/qs.h`
from the installed `include` directory and links the installed `libqs.a` with `-lm` must build
and behave like the programs in `build/bin`.

## 9. Typical use

    make -j8
    make -j8 check
    make install PREFIX=/usr DESTDIR=/tmp/stage
    make DEBUG=1

#!/bin/sh
# Usage: genops.sh OPS_DEF > ops.h
# Writes the operation table header for the expression evaluator to stdout.
set -e
def=${1:?usage: genops.sh OPS_DEF}

function fail(msg) { printf "%s:%d: %s\n", FILENAME, FNR, msg > "/dev/stderr"; bad = 1; exit 1 }
/^[ \t]*#/ || /^[ \t]*$/ { next }
{
    if (NF != 6) fail("expected 6 columns, found " NF)
    if ($3 !~ /^[0-9]+$/ || $4 !~ /^[0-9]+$/) fail("arity and precedence must be numbers")
    if ($5 == "left") a = "QS_LEFT"; else if ($5 == "right") a = "QS_RIGHT"; else if ($5 == "func") a = "QS_FUNC"; else fail("unknown assoc " $5)
    if ($1 in seen) fail("duplicate name " $1)
    seen[$1] = 1
    n++
    name[n] = $1; tok[n] = $2; arity[n] = $3; prec[n] = $4; assoc[n] = a; fn[n] = $6
}
END {
    if (bad) exit 1
    print "/* Generated from src/ops.def by build-aux/genops.sh. Do not edit. */"
    print "#ifndef QS_OPS_H"
    print "#define QS_OPS_H"
    print ""
    print "#include \"qs/expr.h\""
    print ""
    printf "#define QS_OPS_COUNT %d\n\n", n
    print "enum qs_op_id {"
    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) printf "    QS_OP_%s,\n", toupper(name[i])
    print "};"
    print ""
    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) printf "double %s(const double *a);\n", fn[i]
    print ""
    print "#define QS_OPS_TABLE \\"
    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) printf "    { \"%s\", \"%s\", %d, %d, %s, %s }%s\n", name[i], tok[i], arity[i], prec[i], assoc[i], fn[i], (i < n ? ", \\" : "")
    print ""
    print "#endif"
}
' "$def"

# colstat

    colstat [-d DELIM] [-c COLS] [--max-size N] [--version] [FILE]

Reads a delimited text file from `FILE`, or from standard input when `FILE` is missing or `-`,
and prints summary statistics for its columns.

## Options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-d DELIM` | Field delimiter: one character, or the word `tab`. Without `-d`: `,`. |
| `-c COLS` | Comma-separated column names, in the order to report them. A name may repeat. Without `-c`: every column in header order. |
| `--max-size N` | Refuse inputs larger than `N` bytes. `N` is a decimal number with an optional suffix: `k` or `K` (1024), `m` or `M` (1024 * 1024), `g` or `G` (1024 * 1024 * 1024). |
| `--version` | Print `colstat VERSION` and exit 0. |

Options may appear in any order. An unknown option, a missing option value, a delimiter longer than
one character, or an invalid size is a usage error.

## Input

- Records end at `\n` or `\r\n`. Empty lines are ignored.
- The first record is the header and names the columns. Column names are compared exactly
  (case and blanks count). When a name occurs twice in the header, the first occurrence is used.
- A field that starts with `"` is quoted: it runs to the next `"` that is not doubled, `""`
  stands for one `"`, and delimiters and line breaks inside it are part of the field. Any text
  after the closing quote, up to the next delimiter, is appended to the field.
- A record with fewer fields than the header has empty values in the missing columns; extra
  fields are ignored.
- A value is numeric when, after removing spaces and tabs at both ends, it is an optional sign,
  digits with an optional decimal point (at least one digit before or after the point), and an
  optional exponent (`e` or `E`, optional sign, digits). Anything else (empty values, `NA`,
  `inf`, hexadecimal, decimal commas) is not counted.

## Output

One line per selected column, in the selected order:

    NAME: count=N min=... max=... mean=... median=... p90=... stdev=...

- `count` is the number of numeric values. When it is 0 the line ends after `count=0`.
- `mean` is the sum of the values in input order divided by the count.
- `median` is the middle value of the sorted values, or the mean of the two middle values.
- `p90` is the nearest-rank 90th percentile: the value at rank `ceil(0.9 * count)` in ascending order.
- `stdev` is the sample standard deviation (divisor `count - 1`), summed in input order; 0 when the
  count is below 2.
- Numbers are printed like C `printf("%.*g")` with `QS_STATS_PRECISION` significant digits
  (defined in `include/qs/stats.h`).

## Exit status

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Success. |
| 2 | Usage error, an empty input (no header), or a name in `-c` that is not a column. Nothing is printed on standard output. |
| 3 | The input is larger than `--max-size`. Nothing is printed on standard output. |
| 4 | The input cannot be read. |

Error messages go to standard error.

    qcalc [--version] [--ops] [-e EXPR] [FILE]

- With `-e EXPR`, evaluates `EXPR` and prints one line.
- Otherwise reads `FILE` (or standard input when `FILE` is missing or `-`) and evaluates each line.
  A trailing `\r` is removed. Lines that are empty, contain only blanks, or whose first non-blank

Tokens are numbers (digits with an optional decimal point and an optional exponent, or a decimal
point followed by digits), names (a letter or `_` followed by letters, digits or `_`, at most 31
characters), the symbols `+ - * / % ^`, parentheses and commas. Spaces and tabs separate tokens.

| `domain error in 'TOKEN'` | An operation whose result is not a number (for example `sqrt` of a negative value). |
| `overflow in 'TOKEN'` | An operation whose result is infinite. |

Columns count from 1. `%` is the C `fmod` remainder.

0 when every evaluated line succeeded, 1 when any line failed, 2 for usage errors, 4 when the input
cannot be read.

# Usage: golden.sh BINDIR
# Runs every case in tests/golden against the programs in BINDIR. A case NAME has:
#   NAME.cmd     the program name and its arguments, one per line

#   NAME.out     expected standard output

# Prints one line per case and exits 1 when any case fails.
bindir=${1:?usage: golden.sh BINDIR}
dir=$(dirname "$0")/golden
cases=0
failed=0
for cmd in "$dir"/*.cmd; do
    [ -f "$cmd" ] || continue
    name=$(basename "$cmd" .cmd)

    set --

        set -- "$@" "$arg"
    done < "$cmd"

    want_status=0
    [ -f "$dir/$name.status" ] && want_status=$(cat "$dir/$name.status")
    got=$("$bindir/$prog" "$@" < "$input" 2>/dev/null)
    status=$?
    want=$(cat "$dir/$name.out")
    if [ "$status" -eq "$want_status" ] && [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then
        echo "PASS $name"
    else
        echo "FAIL $name (exit $status, expected $want_status)"
        failed=$((failed + 1))
    fi
done

steps.message:
The build now meets `docs/BUILDING.md`. From a clean tree, `make -j8 check` passes in both the release and `DEBUG=1` configurations, with 22 unit tests and 34 golden cases and no failures.

I also ran `make -j8 install DESTDIR=/tmp/st PREFIX=/usr` and checked the installed file list and modes. `qs.pc` records the prefix given at install time. I did not compile a program against the installed headers and `libqs.a`.

I wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

**Makefiles (`mk/*.mk`)**
- **Generated headers:** both `version.h` and `ops.h` now go to `build/gen/qs/`, and every object depends on them.
- **Stale header:** I deleted the hand-written `include/qs/ops.h`. It was out of date: it lacked `hypot` and `clamp`, and its precedence values differed from `src/ops.def`.
- **Link line:** programs link statically, with the objects first, then `libqs.a`, then `-lm`, and they depend on `libqs.a`.
- **Incremental builds:** the compile rules write dependency files (`-MMD -MP`), so changed sources, headers, `VERSION` or `src/ops.def` rebuild what depends on them. Running `make` again with nothing changed does nothing.
- **Flags:** `DEBUG=1` now uses `-O1 -g -DQS_TRACE` as documented. I added a stamp file so switching between plain `make` and `make DEBUG=1` rebuilds everything.
- **`check`:** it now fails if the unit tests or the golden cases fail. Before, the unit test failure was ignored and `tee` hid the golden exit status.
- **`install`:** it installs `qcalc.1`, which was missing, and `version.h`. It creates `qs.pc` at install time so the prefix is the one you pass.

**Source fixes:** every warning is fixed in the code, with no flags or pragmas. They included missing `free` declarations, unused variables and parameters, sign-compare, a missing switch case, fallthroughs in the size parser and `%d` formats under `QS_TRACE`. Beyond the warnings, I renamed `QS_DEBUG` to `QS_TRACE` in the code, and `--max-size` now rejects a value that would overflow. Hand-checked qcalc expressions (precedence, unary minus, error messages, `--ops`) matched `docs/qcalc.md`.
